title: decline / no_show / *_unavailable have no source-state guard in Sitting, Walking and Boarding: a completed or cancelled booking is regressed to reassignment_needed
actor: The assigned partner themselves, authenticated as themselves. app/api/sitting-lifecycle POST puts decline / sitter_unavailable in providerActions (requireProviderOwnership on the booking's own provider_id, bookings.view class permission); the same shape holds for walking-lifecycle and boarding-stays. Only no_show needs bookings.manage. No preview flag, no elevated role, no Ops involvement is needed for the destructive path.
request: Real exported lib functions driven directly over node:sqlite with the product's own DDL. (1) mutateSittingBooking(db,{bookingId,action:'decline',actorId:'PROV-A',idempotencyKey,reason:'sitter fell ill'}); (2) mutateWalkingBooking(db,{bookingId,action:'decline',...,reason:'walker fell ill'}); (3) mutateBoardingStay(db,{stayId,action:'decline',...,reason:'host fell ill'}). Each run twice: once against a booking seeded at status='completed' with its work order / decision / reservation all terminal, and once at status='cancelled'.
response: All six calls returned 200-equivalent success objects, no error thrown. Sitting: {bookingId,status:'ops_escalation',recoveryId:'5e7b77e5-...',bookingPreserved:true}. Walking: {bookingId,status:'ops_escalation',recoveryId:'a78e41f5-...',bookingPreserved:true}. Boarding: {stayId,bookingId,status:'ops_escalation',recoveryId:'30141580-...'}. The literal 'bookingPreserved:true' is returned while the completion is being destroyed. A customer notification row is queued saying 'Your sitter needs to be recovered. PawSpace Operations is protecting the same booking while a replacement is arranged.'
d1_before: SITTING completed: canonical_bookings{id:PS-SIT-completed,status:'completed',provider_id:PROV-A}; provider_work_orders{status:'completed'}; scheduling_assignment_decisions{status:'completed',selected_provider_id:PROV-A}; scheduling_reservations{status:'completed'}. WALKING completed: canonical_bookings{status:'completed'}; work order 'completed'; decision 'completed'; walking_sessions{status:'completed'}. BOARDING completed: canonical_bookings{status:'completed'}; boarding_stays{status:'completed',check_in_status:'complete',check_out_status:'complete'}; decision 'completed'. Same three seeded again at 'cancelled' throughout.
d1_after: SITTING completed -> canonical_bookings.status='reassignment_needed', provider_work_orders.status='recovery_pending', scheduling_assignment_decisions.status='reassignment_needed', scheduling_reservations.status='cancelled', new sitting_recovery_cases{status:'ops_escalation',reason_code:'decline'}. SITTING cancelled -> identical: status='reassignment_needed' (the cancellation is gone). WALKING completed -> booking 'reassignment_needed', work order 'recovery_pending', decision 'reassignment_needed'; walking_sessions kept 'completed' (that UPDATE alone excludes completed/cancelled), so the session says completed while its booking says reassignment_needed. WALKING cancelled -> same. BOARDING completed -> canonical_bookings 'reassignment_needed', boarding_stays 'recovery_pending' but check_in_status stays 'complete' and check_out_status stays 'complete'. BOARDING cancelled -> same. No prior status is written anywhere; the previous value is overwritten in place with no history column and no audit row that records it.
canonical_failure: In all three verticals the decline / *_unavailable / no_show branch reads the booking row and never inspects its status, so a single ordinary partner-authenticated call silently overwrites a committed 'completed' or 'cancelled' booking with 'reassignment_needed' and returns success claiming bookingPreserved:true.
refutation: PARTIAL REFUTATION of the words 'can never be restored' - it is exact for Boarding and for every cancelled booking, and inexact for Sitting/Walking completed. Boarding: with a fully live, KYC-verified, home-verified host seeded, mutateBoardingStay accept DID succeed from recovery_pending (stay -> 'confirmed'), but the accept branch only rewrites the booking when it is in ('confirmed','created'), so canonical_bookings stayed 'reassignment_needed'; check_in then returned 409 'Boarding stay is already checked in' (check_in_status was never reset from 'complete') and check_out returned 409 'Only a checked-in active stay can be checked out'. finalizeBoardingRecoveryAcceptance returned 409 'Replacement host acceptance is required before recovery finalization'. The stay is left permanently at stay='confirmed' / booking='reassignment_needed' with no forward action that accepts either state - a true dead end. Sitting: mutateSittingOps assign_replacement DID succeed on the wrecked completed booking, moving it to 'reassignment_offered' and rewriting canonical_bookings.provider_id from PROV-A to PROV-B; close_recovery then 409'd 'Replacement sitter must accept the recovered booking before Operations can close recovery'. So a forward path to 'completed' exists, but only by handing the already-finished booking to a DIFFERENT sitter who must re-accept, re-submit a care plan, re-check-in and re-check-out - the original completion, its provider attribution and its work order are destroyed either way and cannot be restored. Walking: accept/confirm_handover/start_walk/complete_walk all 409'd from reassignment_needed ('Dog Walking booking is not awaiting walker acceptance', 'Walker acceptance is required before handover', 'Canonical booking must be assigned before a walk starts', 'Only an active Dog Walking session can be completed'), and the session row still reads 'completed', so the same replacement dance is the only route. For a CANCELLED booking in any of the three there is no action anywhere in these modules that writes status back to 'cancelled' - that state is unrecoverable in all three verticals.
blast_radius: Every booking ever completed or cancelled in Sitting, Walking and Boarding stays destructible for as long as the partner keeps their assignment, because nothing in the branch is time-bounded or state-bounded. It needs a deliberate actor but not a privileged one and not a malicious one: the partner app's own 'Can't make it' control fired against a finished job is enough, and the API answers 200 with bookingPreserved:true so neither the partner nor Ops sees an error. Consequences observed in the data: settlement and payout logic keys off status='completed' (the Sitting Ops snapshot raises 'settlement_not_ready' only for completed bookings), so a regressed booking silently drops out of the settlement queue; a regressed cancelled booking re-enters the recovery queue as live work and Ops can offer a cancelled customer's slot to a new provider; capacity is released for a stay that already happened; and in Walking and Boarding the child records (walking_sessions='completed', boarding_stays.check_in_status='complete') now contradict the parent booking, which is what makes Boarding unrecoverable.

title: Concurrent activation of one application mints two provider identities; the orphan can be taken live and assigned bookings with no application and no verification record behind it
risk_category: irreversible corruption of committed state (duplicate identity, unreachable by every governance control)
actor: Two Ops staff with activation authority (or one staff member double-submitting / a retried request), each authenticated normally. Both calls are legitimate; neither actor does anything wrong and neither sees an error.
request: Real harness copied from tests/provider-lifecycle-hardening.test.mjs: readyApplication({verticalKey:'boarding'}) + completeInterviewAndProfile({services:['boarding']}), then every host mandate (aadhaar, house_verification, pan, pet_proofing_photo) driven through runProviderVerification and set to 'verified' so verificationMandateStatus(category:'host').allVerified===true. Then Promise.allSettled([activateProviderUat(db,{applicationId:'POAPP-BOARDING-1',actorEmail:'ops.one@pawspace.in'}), activateProviderUat(db,{applicationId:'POAPP-BOARDING-1',actorEmail:'ops.two@pawspace.in'})]) with the D1 shim yielding 40 microtasks on the 'SELECT ... FROM provider_onboarding_applications WHERE id=?' read so the two calls interleave at the read-mint-write window. Then addProviderToServiceMap({providerId:<orphan>,zoneIds:['blr-east']}) and loadGovernedProviders(db,'blr','blr-east','boarding').
response: BOTH activations fulfilled. Run 1: {providerId:'PROV-0ED28A71-693',status:'activated_uat',...} and {providerId:'PROV-27F9EF53-B52',status:'activated_uat',...}. Run 2: 'PROV-3321CABD-9B0' and 'PROV-FC3CE9A5-224'. No error, no conflict, no warning on either side. addProviderToServiceMap on the orphan returned {providerId:'PROV-0ED28A71-693',zoneIds:['blr-east'],live:true,status:'active'}.
d1_before: provider_onboarding_applications{id:'POAPP-BOARDING-1',provider_id:NULL,status:'profile'}; provider_capacity_profiles: 0 rows for this application; provider_onboarding_activation_runs: 0 rows. provider_verifications holds 4 rows all status='verified' keyed on application_id (the table has NO provider_id column at all - columns are id, application_id, category, verification_type, status, automated, provider_ref, detail_json, updated_by, created_at, updated_at).
d1_after: provider_capacity_profiles: TWO rows - PROV-0ED28A71-693 and PROV-27F9EF53-B52, both city_id='blr', services_json='["boarding"]', zones_json='["blr-east"]', live=0, status='uat_ready'. provider_onboarding_activation_runs: TWO rows, one per provider id, both result='activated_uat'. provider_onboarding_applications.provider_id='PROV-27F9EF53-B52' (last writer wins). SELECT id FROM provider_onboarding_applications WHERE provider_id='PROV-0ED28A71-693' returns NULL - the orphan has no application. After addProviderToServiceMap the orphan row reads live=1, status='active'. loadGovernedProviders(db,'blr','blr-east','boarding') returns ['host_maya_rohan','host_sana','host_arjun_tara','host_priya_dev','PROV-09BAE4B9-0C8'] - the orphan is in the assignable pool.
canonical_failure: activateProviderUat reads application.provider_id, mints PROV-<uuid> when it is empty, inserts provider_capacity_profiles and only then writes provider_id back, with no transaction, no lock and no idempotency key across those steps, so two overlapping activations of one application create two permanent provider identities and the one the application does not end up pointing at is an orphan that is still fully activatable and fully matchable.
refutation: None. Specifically checked and NOT a mitigation: PTJA-P0-05's verifiedMatchingScope() keys on applicationId, not providerId, so BOTH profiles - including the orphan - were written with the full verified scope services_json=["boarding"]. The orphan is not a harmless empty shell; it carries exactly the same matchable services as the legitimate identity. Also checked: SERIALISED double activation is safe (the second call reads the now-populated provider_id and ON CONFLICT-updates the same row) - only the concurrent window duplicates, which is why nothing in the normal test path catches it.
blast_radius: The orphan is unreachable by every control the platform has, because all of them are keyed on the application. Proven directly: with both identities live on the service map, recordManualVerification(applicationId, 'house_verification', status:'failed') - the PTJA-P1-F50 de-listing control - de-listed the BOUND provider (live 1->0, status 'active'->'uat_ready', removed from loadGovernedProviders) and left the ORPHAN live=1, status='active' and still in the assignable pool. So the identity with a failed mandatory house verification stays on the map and can be assigned real boarding stays; revoking KYC, failing a re-inspection, editing the profile (updateActivatedProviderProfile takes an applicationId), or any future suspension keyed on the application all miss it. It also has no verification record reachable from it in either direction, since provider_verifications has no provider_id column, so no audit answering 'what verifications back this provider' can ever be run for it. Nothing deletes it; the duplicate row in provider_capacity_profiles and the duplicate row in provider_onboarding_activation_runs are committed permanently and there is no exported function anywhere that removes a capacity profile. Payouts, performance scoring and recovery shortlists all key on provider_id, so the two identities also split one real person's history.

title: Second expiry of a reservation lease releases capacity but leaves the assignment decision 'assigned' and the provider offer 'pending'
risk_category: silent divergence of committed scheduling records (not destruction - repairable)
actor: Nobody. cleanupExpiredReservationLeases(db) runs unattended at the top of app/api/uat-scheduling operateAssignment (and wherever else it is called), so the divergence appears on its own the next time any request touches scheduling. The only human act in the sequence is an entirely ordinary Ops reassignment of the same schedule group after a first lapsed lease.
request: Real lib function lib/scheduling-reservation-leases.ts cleanupExpiredReservationLeases(db,now) executed three times over node:sqlite with the product's own DDL from app/api/uat-scheduling/route.ts. T1=1770000000000: group SG-LEASE-1 has RES-1 status='assigned' lease_expires_at=T1-1000, decision status='assigned' selected_provider_id='PROV-A', offer status='pending'. Call 1 at T1. Then the group is reassigned exactly as operateAssignment does it (cancel the old rows, insert RES-2 with lease_expires_at=now+SCHEDULING_RESERVATION_LEASE_MS, saveDecision status='assigned', createAssignmentOffer status='pending') at T2=T1+1h. Call 2 at T3=T2+15min+1s. Call 3 at T3+60s.
response: Call 1 returned {groups:1,reservations:1}. Call 2 returned {groups:1,reservations:1} - it reports the same success as a clean release. Call 3 returned {groups:0,reservations:0}. No error at any point.
d1_before: After the reassignment and before the second expiry: scheduling_reservations RES-1 status='cancelled', RES-2 status='assigned' lease_expires_at=1770004500000; scheduling_assignment_decisions{group_id:'SG-LEASE-1',status:'assigned',selected_provider_id:'PROV-A',actor_id:'ops@pawspace.in',reason:'assign'}; provider_assignment_offers{provider_id:'PROV-A',status:'pending',attempt_no:1,response_reason:NULL}; scheduling_reservation_lease_cleanup{group_id:'SG-LEASE-1',reason:'reservation_lease_expired',released_at:1770000000000} - still carrying the FIRST expiry's timestamp.
d1_after: After the second expiry: scheduling_reservations RES-1='cancelled', RES-2='cancelled' (capacity released, 0 live reservations for the group); scheduling_assignment_decisions STILL {status:'assigned',selected_provider_id:'PROV-A',actor_id:'ops@pawspace.in',reason:'assign'} - untouched; provider_assignment_offers STILL {status:'pending',response_reason:NULL} - untouched; scheduling_reservation_lease_cleanup still released_at=1770000000000, no second row. Contrast the FIRST expiry, which did it correctly: decision -> status='expired', actor_id='system:reservation-lease-cleanup', reason='reservation_lease_expired'; offer -> status='cancelled', response_reason='reservation_lease_expired'. A third cleanup pass changes nothing (groups:0) because the predicate requires status='assigned' reservations, which no longer exist - so it never self-repairs.
canonical_failure: scheduling_reservation_lease_cleanup has group_id as PRIMARY KEY and cleanup writes it with INSERT OR IGNORE, so on a group's second lease expiry the marker row keeps the first expiry's released_at; the reservation-cancelling UPDATE has no dependency on that marker and fires, while the decision and offer UPDATEs are both gated on EXISTS(... c.released_at=?) bound to the current now and therefore match nothing and silently do nothing.
refutation: None for the mechanism, but the framing 'irreversible deletion or corruption' does not hold: nothing committed is destroyed. Cancelling the reservations is the intended capacity release; what is left behind are two stale rows, and both are repairable in place - a further Ops reassign overwrites the decision via saveDecision and the offer via createAssignmentOffer (group_id is the offers table's primary key), and the 'cancel' action sets both to 'cancelled'. Also verified that the customer is NOT able to book on the phantom hold: inserting into booking_reservation_confirmation_guards for the group raised ABORT 'reservation_lease_expired_before_booking', so the canonical booking transaction fails closed exactly as designed.
blast_radius: What a customer sees: their checkout is refused, correctly, by the guard trigger - but the refusal reason surfaced upstream is not 'your hold expired'. The confirmation routes check the DECISION first (app/api/sitting-bookings and its siblings reject unless assignment.status==='assigned'), and the decision still reads 'assigned', so the request sails past that check and dies on the next one, the reservation count - a Gate-1 shape error, not an expiry message. What Ops sees: the scheduling board joins scheduling_reservations to scheduling_assignment_decisions and renders the group's decision column as 'assigned to PROV-A, by ops@pawspace.in' while every reservation row underneath it reads 'cancelled' and zero capacity is actually held - the board asserts a provider is holding a slot that is free and re-sellable to anyone. What the partner sees: a live 'pending' offer for that group with no reason recorded, indistinguishable from a real one in any offer listing, and no cancellation notice; the offer's own 3-minute expires_at has long passed so an accept attempt 409s ('Provider offer has expired'), which reads to the partner as a bug rather than a withdrawn offer. Scope: every schedule group that lapses twice - which is the normal shape of a re-offered group, since operateAssignment always writes a fresh 15-minute lease on reassignment. It compounds silently because the cleanup function returns {groups:1,reservations:1} and no error, so no monitor can distinguish a clean release from a half release.
